text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- The Danes' favourite drink is still coffee with an average per head consumption of 200 litres in 1996, Consumption of soft drinks increased to 80 litres per head this year from 50 litres in 1991, mainly at the expense of milk.

--- U.S.-owned music cable television channel MTV has signed a trial three-month, three million crown contract with Danish computer game company Interactive Television Entertainment (ITE). Under the terms of the deal ITE is to deliver MTV a computer game to be shown worldwide.

--- SAS Scandinavian Airlines comes in bottom place for punctuality on domestic services in Denmark in the past few months. Services by competitors Maersk Air, British Airways Express and cooperation partner Cimber Air all depart on time more frequently, according to the latest statistics.

--- The Confederation of Danish Industry expects electricity companies to cut prices by 0.1-0.2 crowns per kilowatt hour in 1997 giving total estimated savings of 100 million crowns to industry. The forecast is based on large profits made on Danish electrical energy exports to Sweden and Norway this year.

--- Denmark's opposition Conservatives and Liberals are to table changes to the 1997 state budget when it enters its third and final reading in parliament later this month, but it is unlikely that they can threaten the Social Democrat-led minority government on the budget following its recent pact with leftist parties.
